riskTone.label: NEUTRAL
riskTone.rationale: FTSE 100 flat with mixed sector moves; US-Iran tension minor drag offset by energy gains; gold recovery signals mild caution.

briefing.briefing: Sterling (GBPUSD) is up +0.13% today, sitting at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range — and because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes FTSE's dollar-earning giants worth less in sterling terms), this is a mild headwind for the index, though the snapshot rates the net FTSE impact as NEUTRAL given the small move. The dominant forces right now are a tug-of-war: Energy is firmly BULLISH (Brent crude up a sharp +3.73%, directly lifting Shell and BP which are top-five index weights), Miners are also BULLISH (copper up +1.63%, a signal of global growth appetite that benefits Rio, Glencore and Anglo American), but Banks are BEARISH (the 10-year gilt yield [the interest rate the UK government pays to borrow for 10 years] fell 6 basis points, compressing the profit margin banks earn between borrowing and lending rates), European peers are soft (DAX -0.28%, EuroStoxx -0.32%), and GBP positioning data shows speculative traders are heavily 'short' sterling [betting it falls] — a crowded trade that historically acts as a contrarian warning. The ORB (Opening Range Breakout — a trade triggered when price pushes beyond the high or low set in the first 15 minutes after the 8am cash open) has already broken DOWNWARD, with the index gapping down 68 points at the open and currently trading at 10,422, well below last night's close of 10,490. That gap has consumed roughly 66% of the average daily range [the typical distance the index travels in a full session, here ~128 points], leaving limited room for further large moves before the session exhausts itself — critical context given that US CPI inflation data [a key measure of how fast prices are rising in America] lands at 13:30 BST today, which the snapshot flags as HIGH-impact and which has caused the bias calculation to be suppressed pending that release. There are no fresh market-moving headlines in the last few hours — the Reuters piece from ~4.5 hours ago on gold recovering pre-CPI confirms markets are already in a holding pattern; the earlier headline (~15 hours ago) noted FTSE was flat as energy gains countered mining losses amid US-Iran tension, explaining some of Brent's spike. Directional bias leans slightly bullish (score +2) on the energy and copper tailwinds, but conviction is LOW: the downside ORB break, a weak European tape, the crowded-short GBP positioning read (flagged bearish for FTSE), and the imminent CPI number all argue for caution. For the ORB trade specifically, the fact that price has already broken down and used two-thirds of the daily range means the short side has limited remaining room, while a CPI surprise in either direction at 13:30 BST could violently reverse or extend the move — this looks like a fakeout/sweep-and-reverse risk environment rather than a clean trend day, and disciplined traders may prefer to stand aside until after the CPI print. In terms of key levels: the overnight high at 10,499 and prior day high at 10,526 are resistance above; the ORB low at 10,447 and overnight low at 10,414 are the key support floors below current price (10,422). Two days from now, UK GDP data (07:00 BST, Wednesday) adds another reason not to be heavily positioned into the week. Today's simple rule: the ORB broke down but the range is mostly used — wait for 13:30 CPI before committing to either side.
